subject: DPA: operational impact and sign-off needed for subprocessor clause
messages:
From: Amanda Park <amanda.park@soluna.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Cc: Soluna Legal <legal@soluna.io>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Redlined DPA (subprocessors)

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal at Soluna reviewed the standard DPA and came back with a couple of redlines around subprocessors and data use that are blocking approval:

- Customer asks: explicit prohibition on sharing customer data with third-party subprocessors without prior written consent.
- Narrower retention limits for analytics logs derived from customer data (30 days instead of 90).

I've attached our redlined DPA (redlined_dpa_v3.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these items or if you need product/security sign-off / an operational exception? This is on the critical path for our PO — would appreciate a quick read and ideally a proposed position by end of week.

Amanda
Amanda Park
Legal Counsel, Soluna Health
attachment: redlined_dpa_v3.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
To: maya.srinivasan@redwood.inference, soojin_lee@redwood.inference
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.inference, priyom_das@redwood.inference, Amanda Park <amanda.park@soluna.io>, Soluna Legal <legal@soluna.io>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Redlined DPA (subprocessors) — need product/security take

Folks — forwarding Soluna's redlines. High-level asks: no subprocessor sharing without prior written consent; shorter analytics retention.

Quick questions for Product/Security:
- Maya: operationally can we support a per-customer opt-out of subprocessors (i.e., an account-level flag that prevents using any third-party hosted components for that tenant), or is the only practical path a dedicated tenancy / on-prem arrangement? Rough estimate of effort and timeline?
- Soojin: security assessment on accepting the clause vs. providing compensating controls (e.g., strict logging, E2E encryption for certain data classes). What evidence would Legal need?

Lauren/Priyom: FYI — Soluna is requesting this for contract signing. If we can't accept, what commercial alternatives do we offer (credits, limited-term exception, dedicated capacity)?

I copied Soluna so they have visibility into where this sits. Goal: get an internal alignment and reply to them with an actionable proposal by Friday.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.inference>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference, soojin_lee@redwood.inference
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.inference, priyom_das@redwood.inference, Amanda Park <amanda.park@soluna.io>, Soluna Legal <legal@soluna.io>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redlined DPA (subprocessors) — product operational impact

Thanks for looping me in. Quick product read:

- Per-customer "no subprocessor" flag is not currently supported. Our runtime relies on a set of managed components (metrics/observability, queueing, certain inference helper services). Enforcing a strict global ban would require either:
  1) Dedicated account isolation (reserved capacity / isolated VPC) so we never route data through multi-tenant helpers, or
  2) Engineering work to make those helpers configurable per-tenant (likely 3-4 sprints across infra & runtime teams because of metrics, KV cache, and monitoring dependencies).

- Shorter analytics retention (30d vs 90d) is easier operationally: we can create a retention policy per-customer in our logging pipeline — low effort (1 sprint).

Recommendation: propose a two-track offer to Soluna: immediate contract concession on retention (we can accept 30d analytics retention) + a commercial option for isolation (Dedicated or Private) as the solution for "no-subprocessor" requests.

If Security signs off on compensating controls (e.g., encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys, strict access logs), we could potentially offer an interim contractual commitment while we queue product work for a configuration flag. That would be a negotiated exception and should be timeboxed.

Tell me desired timelines from Legal; if Soluna needs enforcement quickly we can prioritize the retention change now and surface the isolation option formally.

Maya
Product Lead, Serving Runtime

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
To: maya.srinivasan@redwood.inference, rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.inference, priyom_das@redwood.inference, Amanda Park <amanda.park@soluna.io>, Soluna Legal <legal@soluna.io>
Date: Wed, 06 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redlined DPA (subprocessors) — security assessment

Appreciate the context. From Security's perspective:

- Absolute ban on subprocessors is high friction operationally and will push customers to Dedicated/Private. We can accept a contractual clause that requires prior written consent for using new subprocessors plus a 30-day notice for existing ones, provided we deliver the following artifacts:
  * Current subprocessor inventory (see attached CSV stub).
  * A short attestation describing encryption controls, access review cadence, and how we segregate customer data in multi-tenant services.
  * SOC 2 report (we already have a SOC 2 Type II; provide link).

- For analytics retention reduction to 30 days, Security has no objection — lower retention reduces risk.

If Legal wants to accept a temporary exception in writing, we recommend:
  - Timeboxed exception (90 days) during which Product teams will deliver a configurable per-tenant control or customer migration path to Dedicated.
  - Mandatory use of customer-managed keys (KMS) where feasible for particularly sensitive data types.

I'll coordinate the inventory export and provide the attestation by Tue 2026-05-11.

Soojin
Director, Security & Compliance
attachment: subprocessor_inventory.csv (text/csv)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
To: Amanda Park <amanda.park@soluna.io>, Soluna Legal <legal@soluna.io>
Cc: maya.srinivasan@redwood.inference, soojin_lee@redwood.inference, lauren_bishop@redwood.inference, priyom_das@redwood.inference
Date: Fri, 09 May 2026 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed position on DPA redlines (next steps)

Amanda / Soluna team — thanks for the redline and for the patience while we reviewed internally. Summary of our proposed position:

1) Analytics retention: we can accept 30-day retention for analytics/derived logs. We'll update the DPA language to reflect that and provide an operational SLA around deletion.

2) Subprocessors: we cannot accept an unconditional, permanent ban on subprocessors in our hosted service. Options we can offer:
   - Dedicated/Private deployment: full isolation, no shared subprocessors (recommended for Soluna if a permanent ban is required).
   - Timeboxed contractual exception: Redwood will commit in writing to not add new subprocessors without prior consent for 90 days while we deliver a roadmap for a more configurable control. During that period, we will provide the subprocessor inventory and a security attestation.

3) Compensating controls: Security will provide an inventory and attestation by Tue 2026-05-11 and will surface the SOC 2 report and KMS options where applicable. Product estimates a multi-sprint effort to add per-tenant configurability (targeting a Q3 roadmap slot); we can prioritize sooner under a commercial commitment.

Next steps we propose:
- Legal (Soluna + Redwood) to confirm whether the 90-day timeboxed exception is acceptable.
- If accepted, Redwood Security will upload the inventory and attestation and Legal will get a draft clause from our team for DocuSign.
- If Soluna requires full removal of subprocessors immediately, we should discuss Dedicated deployment pricing and timeline.

I've looped in Lauren (sales ops) and Priyom (pre-sales) to coordinate commercial options. Please let me know your preference and I'll get the draft clause over.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
